fields.h1: Build a Home Inspection Form That Becomes the Report
fields.hero_description: Build a home inspection form that rates each item, puts a photo on every defect, and saves inspections to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Inspection Form Has to Carry
fields.features_subheading: Paper home inspection forms stop at the checkmark. These parts carry each finding into the report a client reads.
fields.feature_1:
Items grouped by system

List the roof, foundation, electrical, plumbing, heating, and cooling items under their own headings. The inspector covers one system at a time and skips nothing between rooms.
fields.feature_2:
One rating on every item

Give each item the same choices, such as Inspected, Not Inspected, Not Present, or Deficient. An item left blank stops the form from submitting, and the report never shows a gap.
fields.feature_3:
Photos and notes on each deficiency

Mark an item Deficient and the form asks for a photo and a note before moving on. The client sees the lifted shingle or the stained ceiling right next to the finding it belongs to.
fields.feature_4:
A report the client opens that night

Submit the inspection and the app builds a report page with deficient items listed first. The buyer and the buyer's agent get a link by email, and each finding opens to its photos.
fields.feature_5:
Every inspection in your own database

Each inspection becomes a record you can search by address, inspector, or date. Pull up last year's report when a client calls back, or export the rows when you review the season.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to GitHub

Export the full code of your inspection app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can host it on your own servers or connect it to the scheduling tool you use.

fields.tab_content_1:
Of 52 items, the three deficient ones carry photos

Marcus Reid inspects a 1987 ranch house for Ridgeline Home Inspections on a tablet. He rates 52 items, and three come back Deficient: lifted shingles, a stained subfloor under the kitchen sink, and a double-tapped breaker. Each has a photo, and the buyer and her agent get the report link that evening.
fields.tab_content_2:
After four showings, Birch Court has the most red flags

Over two weekends, Priya Nair fills the same 20-question checklist at four houses she might buy, and the form counts red flags at each. The house at 14 Birch Court collects five, including a furnace from 1998 and a soft spot in the bathroom floor. It drops to the bottom of her shortlist.
fields.tab_content_3:
On move-in day, the tenant signs off on all nine rooms

Before keys change hands, a manager at Harbor Lane Properties walks unit 4B with the new tenant. Each of the nine rooms gets a condition rating and a photo. A cracked bathroom tile is logged as fair, with two photos. The tenant signs on the manager's phone, and the report is saved to the lease record for move-out.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before a buyer reads it, a hazard report gets a second look

Keystone Inspection Group runs five inspectors, and any report with an item marked as a safety hazard waits for Ana Ruiz, the lead inspector, before it reaches the client. This morning, the report on 9 Larch Street flags exposed wiring in the attic. It sits in her queue while the other four reports go out.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Home Inspection Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a home inspection form that rates every item and documents each defect, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who reads the finished report before listing a single item. A buyer wants plain findings with photos. A property manager wants a condition record the tenant signs. The reader sets how deep each section goes and which items can stay off the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Group the items by system, in the order you walk the house, so nothing is missed. List the components you check under each heading, from the roof and attic down to the foundation.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick one rating scale and use it on every item. Texas inspectors work with four ratings on the state's report form: Inspected, Not Inspected, Not Present, and Deficient. A home inspection form PDF from another state may label them differently. Settle the labels before you build.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Make a photo and a short note required whenever an item is marked Deficient. Say where the photo was taken, such as the north slope of the roof or the main electrical panel. A client reading it weeks later should find the problem without calling you.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your systems, items, rating scale, and photo rules into the prompt. Emergent builds the form, the report page, and the database behind them. Add a rule for who hears about safety hazards, and change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set who receives each finished report. Buyers and their agents usually get it by email. A tenant gets a copy of the signed condition record, and a report with a safety hazard can go to your lead inspector first. Keep every inspection on the property's record.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Walk your own house with the form before a paid job. Mark two items Deficient, attach photos, and submit. Open the finished page as a client would, check that the deficient items come first, and time how long the whole walk-through took.

faq_plan.q: What is the biggest red flag in a home inspection?
faq_plan.ref: What is the biggest red flag in a home inspection?

prov.original: What is the biggest red flag in a home inspection?

faq_plan.a: Treat a safety hazard as the biggest red flag: Texas rules count a condition that constitutes a hazard to life, limb, or property as a deficiency. Add a hazard checkbox beside the Deficient rating on your home inspection form and sort those findings above every other item in the report.

faq_plan.q: How can I create an inspection report?
faq_plan.ref: How can I create an inspection report?

prov.original: How can I create an inspection report?

faq_plan.a: Build the form and the report as one app: each rating and photo the inspector enters then shows up in the client's report without retyping. Emergent's AI form builder builds that app from a plain-English description of your checklist, and you change it later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find a free template for a home inspection report?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I find a free template for a home inspection report?

prov.original: Where can I find a free template for a home inspection report?

faq_plan.a: You can build one on Emergent for free, since the free tier covers building and publishing. Describe the systems you inspect and the rating each item gets, then run the result on your own house before a paid job.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find inspection report templates?
faq_plan.ref: Where can I find inspection report templates?

prov.original: Where can I find inspection report templates?

faq_plan.a: Start with the form your state publishes: in Texas, an inspection for a prospective buyer or seller of a one-to-four family home must be reported on the state's Form REI 7-6. Landlords who inspect at move-in can file the condition report on the same record as the rental agreement form the tenant signed.

faq_plan.q: What should home inspection forms include?
faq_plan.a: Home inspection forms should open with the property address and the date of the inspection. Add a field for any item you could not reach, with the reason, such as an attic hatch blocked by storage boxes. Close with the inspector's signature, which the app can capture on the tablet.

faq_plan.q: How do I adapt a home inspection form template to my own inspections?
faq_plan.a: Cut the items you never inspect from the home inspection form template and add the ones your area needs, such as a sump pump or a private well. Reorder the sections to follow the route you walk, and the form never sends you back across the house. If you start from a home inspection form pdf, copy its item list into your prompt and leave its layout behind.

faq_plan.q: How do you write an inspection report?
faq_plan.ref: How do you write an inspection report?

prov.original: How do you write an inspection report?

faq_plan.a: Write each finding as the condition you saw plus the action you recommend. A good one reads: "Water stain on the hallway ceiling below the upstairs bath; have a plumber check the drain line." Use words a buyer can act on, and leave out code citations the client cannot check. For a rental, file the move-in report on the tenant's record next to their tenant screening form.

faq_plan.q: What does a housing inspection consist of?
faq_plan.ref: What does a housing inspection consist of?

prov.original: What does a housing inspection consist of?

faq_plan.a: As the Texas standards of practice define it, a real estate inspection is a limited visual survey and basic performance evaluation of the systems and components of a building using normal controls. Inspectors need not inspect anything hidden or concealed, so give each section a field for what could not be seen, such as a furnace behind a locked panel.

faq_plan.q: What does a home inspection form look like?
faq_plan.ref: what a home inspection form looks like
faq_plan.a: Texas sets one out in its rules: a row per item with check boxes for the rating, and the findings explained in the corresponding section in the body of the report form. Put the property address, the inspection date, and your name in a header above the rows. Describe that layout in a prompt and Emergent builds it with a photo field beside each rating.

faq_plan.q: Are there do it yourself home inspection forms for buyers?
faq_plan.ref: do it yourself home inspection forms
faq_plan.a: Yes, a buyer's checklist works as a do it yourself home inspection form, scoring each house you tour on the same items. Emergent builds one from a plain-English prompt, and you add items by prompting as your list grows.
